So many comments sound apocalyptic when they face inconveniences like inflation. See this recent post by a Polish guy:

https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49905487

Meanwhile, the Tigray war in Ethiopia may have killed as many as 600k, yet it barely registered in our public conversation. The same goes for Sudan.

Attention is a weird beast.

Calling inflation an inconvenience is certainly an opinion. How many people will die across the world because they have to choose between healthcare, food, and rent?

Really bad inflation is obviously a full human catastrophe.

The absolute meltdown post-COVID where we traded moderate inflation in exchange for not having the economy basically seize up was, for most people on HN, an inconvenience.

lukan · Oct 3, 2026

"Attention is a weird beast."

Not nice, but somewhat rational? Inflation where you live affects you directly. A massacre somewhere far away usually not so much.

(But yes, all is connected, people fleeing the wars, then bringing their traumatas with them, etc)

We give attention to things that deserve our attention, i.e., things that affect us. The war in Ethiopia scores very low on that list, to the point of almost complete irrelevance.
